Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:7: And in the Tikkunim (page 25b) it appears that one must direct his intent to the Name mentioned even in the performance of a commandment. There Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained the matter of YHVH, that it is Yud-Heh, fear and love, and Vav-Heh, Torah and commandment, and he said: Vav - this is the Torah, resting in the mouth and in the breath of the mouth, for Chokhmah and Binah are hidden in the brain and heart, in love and fear, and Torah without fear and love does not fly upward, and so on. Heh, small, in the image of man - through it YHVH is completed, and it is the Heh, the holy Malchut, which is the commandment, the performance of the precepts, resting in the two hundred forty-eight limbs; and Torah and commandment, concerning them it is said "and the revealed things are for us" - Vav-Heh are revealed to us and to our children forever - and a commandment without fear and love cannot ascend before YHVH, which is the sum of all; above all, Adam, Yud-Heh-Vav-Heh spelled with alefs, thought that ascends to Ein Sof - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:8: And the intent of Rashbi, peace be upon him, is to explain that the Name YHVH should always be complete, whether in the occupation with Torah or in the performance of a commandment. And therefore, in the occupation with Torah, it is Heh, "resting in the mouth and in the breath of the mouth" - that is, the mouth is Heh, the breath of the mouth is Vav - and the explanation of the matter is that the mouth is Heh, since in the mouth are the five points of articulation through which speech is cut, and Vav, "the breath of the mouth," is the voice emerging from the windpipe within which are the rings, as explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Parashat Pinchas, pages 235a-b), and therefore it is explained in the Tikkunim (page 145b) that voice and speech are Vav-Heh; and in fear and love, which are Yud-Heh - behold, YHVH.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:9: And likewise concerning the commandment [mitzvah], Rashbi, peace be upon him, was precise in his wording when he said, "Heh, small, in the image of man - through it YHVH is completed." What is the meaning of "the image of man" here? And then he went back and said, "it is the commandment, the performance of the precepts," and so on. Rather, the matter is as Rashbi explained there (page 131b): that "mitzvah" is the completion of YHVH, for M-Tz in the Atbash cipher is Yud-Heh, and YHVH transforms in Atbash to Mem-Tzadi-Peh-Tzadi, and so on, as explained there - behold, in the word "mitzvah" itself is YHVH. And this is because the Shechinah, in her, all of Atzilut is figured, for she is comprised of ten [sefirot], and this is why she is called "the image of man." And therefore he said, "it is the commandment." And to be precise about how YHVH is found in her, he elaborated in his wording and said, "it is the commandment, the performance of the precepts, which rests in the two hundred forty-eight limbs" - meaning that the reality of the performance is from her, which is Heh, and she rests in the two hundred forty-eight limbs, which is Vav - for the two hundred forty-eight limbs of man are from the side of the male, and likewise the two hundred forty-eight positive commandments are from the right, corresponding to the two hundred forty-eight limbs, since the male inclines to the right; and the three hundred sixty-five sinews correspond to the negative commandments, from the left, since the female inclines to the left. And "a commandment without fear and love cannot ascend," and so on - behold, YHVH, for fear and love are Yud-Heh.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:10: And the Name Yud-Heh comes by transposition through Atbash in the word "mitzvah" - the reason being that Vav-Heh are the revealed, as the verse says, "and the revealed things," while love and fear are hidden in the brain and heart, and therefore they come as hidden, through the transposition of letters. And therefore, if a commandment lacks love and fear, the commandment is not completed such that YHVH would rest in it and it would ascend above. It follows that whether in Torah or in a commandment, YHVH must be completed through fear and love, as explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:11: Afterward he must direct his intent to the secret of thought, which is Yud-Heh-Vav-Heh spelled with alefs, to ascend all the way to Ein Sof, and through this Name, Ein Sof rests and its light spreads through the attributes - and for this reason Rashbi, peace be upon him, called it in the Tikkunim (page 17a) "the watering of the tree from within" - and therefore one must direct his intent to this Name in order to draw the light of the blessed Ein Sof into His attributes. And see in the Tikkunim how greatly Rashbi, peace be upon him, extolled the virtue of this Name.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:12: And this is the essence of everything: to repair first the supernal attributes, which are His blessed thrones, in order to cause the light of the blessed Emanator, Ein Sof, to rest upon them - and the essential intent of a person's thought in his prayer and his Torah is to always direct his intent to the essence of all things that sustains everything, the blessed Ein Sof. And so Rashbi, of blessed memory, explained (Zohar, Parashat Vayakhel, page 213b): through these secrets a person can cleave to his Master - with will, by directing the heart to know the dominion of Chokhmah in the supernal secret; when he serves his Master in prayer, he should attach his will like a fire to a coal, to unify those lower firmaments on the side of holiness, to crown them with one lower name, and from there onward to unify those inner supernal firmaments, so that they all become one within that supernal firmament that stands over them; and while his mouth and lips move, his heart should direct its will to ascend higher and higher, to unify everything in the secret of secrets, where all wills and thoughts are anchored, in the secret that stands in Ein Sof - this, in every single prayer, to direct body and soul to this, every single day, to crown his days in the secret of the supernal days through his service - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:13: And after we have explained the essence of the holiness of thought, we must explain what preparations are needed for the holiness of thought, so that thought may cleave to Him, blessed be He, and to His Torah always, whether he is engaged in his work, whether walking, lying down, or rising - and that his love for Him, blessed be He, never separate from him, just as His blessed love cleaves to us always.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:14: And we say that just as the secret of the supernal thought rests upon the attributes only through the repair of the attributes that are below it, which serve as a throne for it - as is known, that when there is a blemish in the attributes, Imma withdraws from the [lower] structure, and all the more so Chokhmah, and when the Mother returns to the children, which is called teshuvah [repentance/return], Chokhmah too returns - so, in the reality of the holiness of thought, a person does not sanctify his thought to cleave to his God except after he first sanctifies all his limbs and purifies them through proper repentance, and afterward sanctifies them, as we shall explain below, with God's help, in detail, the several kinds of holiness - and they are included in the holiness of sight, hearing, smell, and speech, which the Tikkunim and the Ra'aya Meheimna explained as corresponding to the Name YHVH. And afterward he sanctifies four others corresponding to the Name Adonai, which are touch [with the hands], movement, pleasure [in the covenant], walking - and they explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, page 99a) that this is touch with the hands, movement in the body, pleasure in the covenant, walking with the feet, and he wrote, in these words: and some say, pleasure with the hands, use of the covenant - and all of it is true - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:15: And once all the vessels of the body are pure and holy, thought will rest within them - but when there is a blemish on any side of the limbs, there is a defect there, for "whoever has a blemish shall not approach" (Leviticus 21:18), and the soul departs entirely, and that husk rests there, and it confuses a person's thought in his prayer and his Torah, and it is impossible for him to have any cleaving at all. And especially if his tongue is blemished by slander or the like, for the tongue is the ladder for the ascent of Torah and prayer, and therefore the evil thought confuses it so that he does not perform a unification through it. And similarly with the other blemishes - being blemished, he cannot unify in his prayer, for prayer is the drawing-near and unification of the attributes through the Cause of Causes, and the Cause of Causes rests only upon a repaired throne.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:16: And especially concerning what we explained in the Gate of Love (chapter 2), that the essence of a person's cleaving to his Maker is the cleaving of his soul to the root of life, as explained concerning the love that depends on kisses - see there - and when the soul is blemished, there is an external force there, and it is impossible for it to cleave to the supernal light. But once the soul is properly repaired, it becomes a throne for the supernal spirituality, and it can cleave to the soul of all, in which is the essential cleaving. And for this necessity we copied several teachings of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Gate of Fear, chapters 9 and 10 - see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:17: And as a general rule, a person sanctifies his limbs and purifies them through purity and holiness, as explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Parashat Pinchas, page 245b), whose wording we copied above in chapter 4 - namely, purity from within and holiness from without - and there Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that these two are acquired through the occupation with Torah. However, in what we wrote in the Gate of Love, chapter 8, concerning purity - that the essence of purity is through fire, and one who sits in fasting purifies himself through the boiling of his fat and blood, melted by the fire that weakens his body - yet our Rabbis, of blessed memory, also explained (Ta'anit 11a-b) that one who sits in fasting is called holy - it follows that its essence is holiness, and this holiness is the right, as it is written (Proverbs 11:17), "a man of kindness benefits his own soul" - see what we wrote. And purity, it is said, has its essence through immersion in a mikveh, as we elaborated above in chapter 8, and it is somewhat fitting to call it "purity from within," for through this the soul is purified from within. And these two things are absolutely necessary for a penitent, for since he is blemished, the occupation with Torah will not avail to purify and sanctify him, for "to the wicked, God said, what have you to do with declaring My statutes" (Psalms 50:16) - and therefore he must first purify himself through immersion, and afterward sanctify himself through fasting, to afflict himself in place of what he enjoyed, as we shall elaborate in the Gate of Repentance, with God's help - and afterward, purity and holiness through the words of Torah will avail him, and Torah will complete for him purity and holiness, for if he is not occupied with Torah, what use is all his repentance, and it turns out that he lacks purity and holiness in full completeness as fitting. Behold, these are the two general aspects for acquiring holiness.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:18: Further, for the acquisition of holiness, the holiness of place is needed, as we find mentioned in the Torah, Parashat Acharei Mot (Leviticus 16:24), "a holy place." And there are two aspects to this: either the place is made holy through the occupation with Torah and prayer, such as a study hall or synagogue, or it is holy in that it is a place separated and set apart from people - and a place solitary from people is a great preparation for cleaving. Therefore the early sages would separate themselves from settled places, and were called the band of solitaries, as the pious author of Chovot HaLevavot brings (Gate of Trust, chapter 4; cf. Gate of Abstinence, chapter 3) - and this is one of the conditions of abstinence, to desire solitude, for through this he shows in his soul that he has no connection at all with the people of this world, as is truly the case after his passing - and therefore, from now on, he shows the alienation of his soul in this world, and does not wish to cleave to anything but his blessed God, to whom he shall cleave in the future with an essential cleaving, if he merits it.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:19: And so he wrote in Chovot HaLevavot (Gate of Trust, ibid.) concerning a certain ascetic who entered a certain land to teach its inhabitants divine service, and found them all wearing garments of one color, and he saw their graves near the doors of their houses, and he did not see any woman among them, and he asked them, and they answered him about each matter as explained there in Chovot HaLevavot. And to the third matter, that he did not see a woman among them, they answered him: as for what you saw, that we separated from the women and children - know that we designated for them a nearby town, and one of us, when he needs something from their affairs, goes to them, completes his need, and returns to us - because we saw what would come upon us from the distraction of the heart and the great loss and the great toil and burden in their proximity, and the rest from all this is in distancing ourselves from them, choosing the affairs of the World to Come and despising this world.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:20: And so we find that Elisha the prophet had a holiness of place as a preparation for his holiness, in what the Shunammite woman did for him, as it is written (2 Kings 4:9-10), "behold now, I know that this is a holy man of God who passes by us continually; let us make a small upper chamber, and let us set for him there a bed, a table, a chair, and a lamp" - and behold, because of his holiness a preparation of place was needed, namely a small upper chamber, which is a place somewhat separated from people, along with the more necessary natural preparations that people commonly use, namely a bed, table, chair, and lamp - which is the abstinence of the middle path, as the pious author of Chovot HaLevavot wrote (Gate of Abstinence, chapter 3) concerning the three groups of ascetics, and those who are solitary in their own homes are the second group, which is closer to Torah - see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:21: Behold, two aspects of the holiness of place. And if it is possible for both to be together, such as a person's solitude in his study hall or synagogue, how good is his portion, for he will certainly acquire extra holiness for his soul. And so they said, of blessed memory (Yalkut Tehillim, remez 872): the Holy One, blessed be He, said, whoever is occupied with Torah and acts of kindness and is regularly found in the synagogue, it is as though he redeemed Me and My children from among the nations of the world - to this point. And his saying "regularly found in the synagogue" indicates constancy in the synagogue, for just as other people, when sought, are known to be found at the places where they habitually sit most of the day, and there they are sought, so this person is found most of the time of the day in the synagogue, to the point that when a person asks his fellow, where is so-and-so to be found, they will answer him that he is found in the synagogue - and he should learn from what was commanded of the High Priest, "and from the sanctuary he shall not go out" (Leviticus 21:12) - along these lines, whoever wishes to sanctify himself shall sanctify himself in the holy place, the synagogue or the study hall.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:22: Nevertheless, solitude is good when combined with acquiring a companion, for they said, of blessed memory (Berachot 63b), "a sword is upon the boasters [badim], and they shall become fools" (Jeremiah 50:36), and so on, as shall be explained, with God's help; and they said, of blessed memory, in the Sifrei (Yalkut Bamidbar, remez 976), on the verse (Ecclesiastes 4:9), "two are better than one" - from here they said, a person should acquire a companion for himself, to read with him, to study with him, to eat with him, and to reveal his secrets to him - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:23: And the way of abstinence and holiness fitting for Torah scholars who separate from their wives from Sabbath to Sabbath is that they choose for themselves a special house, separate from the house in which they dwell with their wives, and arrange their livelihood and that of their households for one day a week - and in this they conduct themselves with the holiness of speech and the other holinesses to be explained, for as long as a person is preoccupied going out and coming in the marketplace, he will not avoid slander, or anger, or at least he will sin through the sight of his eyes - and abstinence in a special house saves a person from all this. This is the straight path that whoever wishes to sanctify himself should choose.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:24: Further, among the things that add holiness and aid the holiness of thought is when a person fulfills the commandments of tzitzit and tefillin in their performance and their intent, as fitting. Concerning the commandment of tzitzit, holiness is explicitly mentioned in the Torah (Numbers 15:40), "so that you may remember and do all My commandments, and be holy to your God." And they said, of blessed memory, in the Sifrei, in these words: "so that you may remember and do" - to make a remembrance like the deed. "And be holy" - this is the holiness of all the commandments; or is it only the holiness of tzitzit? What is the passage speaking of - the holiness of all the commandments? Rabbi says, this is the holiness of tzitzit; or is it only the holiness of all the commandments? When it says (Leviticus 19:2), "you shall be holy," the holiness of all the commandments is already stated - so what does Scripture teach by saying "and be holy"? This is the holiness of tzitzit, teaching that tzitzit adds holiness to Israel - to this point. Behold, it is explicit, according to Rabbi, that tzitzit adds holiness.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:25: And it is possible to say the reason, as explained above in chapter 4 from the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, that all holiness is from without, and as it is written (Parashat Chayei Sarah, beginning of page 125b), "the assistance of his Master surrounds him and he is called holy" - and the reason was explained there. Now, the commandment of tzitzit is a commandment in which a person wraps himself, and the commandment, in its holiness, surrounds him from all around, and therefore it adds holiness.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:26: And so too they called the commandment of tefillin "holiness," of blessed memory, in saying (Megillah 26b) concerning the straps, that they are holy implements, while the tallit is an implement of a commandment. And so is the wording of Rashbi, peace be upon him, concerning tzitzit and tefillin, distinguishing between "commandment" and "holiness" several times - that the tefillin are a supernal holiness greater than the tzitzit, since the tzitzit is called a commandment and the tefillin holiness.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:27: And the commentators, of blessed memory (Rabbeinu Yonah, Berachot 8a in the pages of the Rif), agreed that the placement of the tefillin on the arm opposite the heart, and on the head, is in order to subjugate to the Holy One, blessed be He, the brain and the heart, which are the primary limbs in a person, upon which life depends, and upon which thoughts depend, as explained at the beginning of this chapter - and the intent is that through the holiness of the twenty-one mentions [of the divine Name] written in the hand-tefillin and twenty-one in the head-tefillin, which correspond to "Ehyeh Asher Ehyeh," as explained in the Tikkunim (page 27b). And there is no doubt that when the mentions in the tefillin are written with the intent that Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in Parashat Vayikra (page 11b) and Parashat Acharei Mot (page 65b), and likewise the repair of the boxes in their squareness and their stitching properly, and the straps and knots properly - that thoughts are purified and a person's thought cleaves to YHVH, for the tefillin are in the place of thought.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:28: And since these two commandments are relevant to the topic we are engaged in, let us speak of them what is found in the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, relevant to the intent of the commandment - for one who performs the commandment with intent is not the same as one who performs it without intent, for through intent one gives the commandment an ascent, that it may ascend above, as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (Tikkunei Zohar, page 25b), whose wording we copied, that he said, "a commandment without fear and love cannot ascend before," and so on. And through knowledge of the commandment's intent, one places in his heart fear and love, by knowing what repair that commandment effects - but if he does not know its intent, the tefillin are found on his brain and arm like mere stones, and they do not arouse in his heart the awakening of fear and love.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:29: Concerning the tallit itself, it is proper from the outset to strive that it be of wool, and the Nimukei Yosef, peace be upon him, elaborated in the minor laws of the Rif, of blessed memory, that the Geonim and most commentators agreed on this, and he wrote at the end of his words, of blessed memory: therefore one should make only a fringed tallit of wool, to fulfill through it the biblical commandment of tzitzit, and I have already so taught the public and the custom has spread this way - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:30: And by way of the plain meaning, the intent of wrapping in tzitzit is to teach a person to remember all the commandments through seeing the techelet [sky-blue thread], as it is said (Numbers 15:39), "and you shall see it and remember all the commandments of the LORD." And how does the techelet indicate their remembrance? This may be understood from what our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Chullin 89a), where it was taught: Rabbi Meir used to say, why is techelet different from all other dyes? Because techelet resembles the sea, and the sea resembles the sky, and the sky resembles the Throne of Glory, as it is said (Exodus 24:10), "and under His feet was like a paved work of sapphire stone," and it is written (Ezekiel 1:26), "like the appearance of a sapphire stone was the likeness of a throne" - to this point. And although this teaching contains a secret, as explained at the end of Parashat Shelach Lecha (Zohar, page 175b), nevertheless, by the plain meaning, it alludes to the quarry of souls, which are from the Throne of Glory, as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said, "the souls of the righteous are hewn from beneath the Throne of Glory" - and when a person remembers the root of his soul, that it is from the Throne, and there his soul shall return, as it is written (Ecclesiastes 12:7), "and the spirit shall return to God who gave it" - and "ha-kisei" [the throne] has the same numerical value as "Elohim" - he will come to fulfill the commandments, and sanctify himself with the holiness of the supernal beings, and separate from the desires of the world. And this is (Numbers 15:39), "that you not go about after your heart and after your eyes, after which you go astray, so that you may remember," and so on, "and be holy to your God" - and the intent in saying "to your God" is that to Him you shall cleave in the end, after the matter perishes, and God rests upon the Throne, and there the Seraphim say "holy."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:31: And it is possible that for this reason it was made from the blood of the chilazon [snail], for the chilazon would emerge once every seventy years, as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained (Menachot 44a), to allude to the days of our years, which are seventy years (Psalms 90:10). And therefore it is explained that all colors are good in a dream except the color of techelet, which indicates strict judgment, being the ultimate purpose of all, the judgment of souls, as explained in the Zohar (Parashat Terumah, page 152a, at the end), in these words: all colors are good in a dream except techelet, as has been said, because it is the throne for judging the judgments of souls, and so on - see there. And this is the reason for "and you shall see it and remember," and so on, as explained there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:32: And it appears to me that this secret is alluded to in the passage of tzitzit, in the words (Numbers 15:39) "ve-hayah lachem le-tzitzit," whose end-letters spell "ha-met" [the dead], for the matter of remembering the tzitzit is to remember the day of death through the chilazon, as explained. And further, "u-re'item oto u-zechartem," whose end-letters have the numerical value of "Elohim," which totals the same as "ha-kisei" [the throne] - namely the throne by which they judge cases of capital judgment [of souls].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:33: And in the Zohar, at the end of Parashat Shelach Lecha (page 175b), it is explained that the entire commandment of tzitzit is a testimony, to testify for a person concerning the service of his Creator - it says there, how many witnesses did the Creator make to testify for a person, and it says concerning the matter of tzitzit: he wraps himself in the wrapping of the commandment on the four corners of his garment - four kings go forth to meet the four, four true witnesses of the King hang from the four corners.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:34: And this wording is from Sifra DeTzniuta, chapter 5, and this is his wording, at the end of Parashat Terumah (page 179a): four kings go forth to meet the four, upon which hang, like grapes in a cluster, seven runners bound to them, testifying testimony yet not remaining in their place - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:35: And all this teaching is explained there at the end of Parashat Shelach Lecha, where it says that the seven runners mentioned are the seven windings of the techelet thread, which one must wind around each and every corner, or increase up to thirteen - whoever adds should not add beyond them, whoever reduces should not reduce below seven. And Rabbi Yitzchak said further there, seven windings, because it [the Shechinah] is the seventh of all, certainly, for she is blessed from the other six through the hand of the Righteous One [Yesod]; and if there are thirteen, they are as established, thirteen measures [of mercy] - and this is the opening of them all.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:36: And he said further there: and we have learned, Yesod and its root are crowned together in the King, and this is the remembrance and the opening for all the other crowns, as it is written (Psalms 118:19), "open for me the gates of righteousness," and it is written, "this is the gate of the LORD," and so on, and it is written (Numbers 15:39), "and you shall see it and remember all the commandments of the LORD," to include in this all the other crowns - and therefore they testify testimony yet do not remain in their place, because it is a commandment, and we have learned that implements of a commandment are cast aside [once used].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:37: Further there, Rabbi Yitzchak said, these threads show how they hang from here and from there to the four directions of the world from this place, and it rules over all in the secret of the heart, for it is the heart of the whole world, and the heart of the supernal beings, and it depends on the supernal heart, and everything is in the heart that emerges from the supernal Chokhmah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:38: Further there, Rabbi Yehudah said, the Holy One, blessed be He, said: whoever wishes to walk after My fear shall walk after this heart and after the eyes that stand upon it. Which are these eyes? As it is said (Psalms 34:16), "the eyes of the LORD are toward the righteous." But you shall not go about after your heart and after your eyes - why? Because you go astray after them - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:39: We find, from the sum of the teaching's words, that there are four tzitziyot, four witnesses, and likewise seven windings, seven witnesses, as it says in Sifra DeTzniuta, "seven runners testify testimony." And the secret of these witnesses is well explained in the words of Rabbi Yehudah, who said, which are these eyes, as it is said, "the eyes of the LORD are toward the righteous" - and these are the eyes of Ze'ir [Anpin] explained in the Zohar (Parashat Naso, page 136b), where it says: from those colors that are revealed emerge seven eyes of watching that emerge from the black of the eye - this is what is written (Zechariah 3:9), "upon one stone are seven eyes" - what is "one stone"? The black of the eye. From the red emerge seven runners that support the left side, and blaze with fire toward the north side, and unite to spread through the world, to reveal the ways of the wicked - this is what is written (ibid. 4:10), "these seven are the eyes of the LORD, roaming through all the earth." From the green emerge seven pure ones bound to the south side, and unite to spread through the world to reveal deeds, as it is written (Job 34:21), "for His eyes are upon the ways of man," and so on - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:40: We find that when a person contemplates the allusion of these witnesses, standing and testifying against him at every time and every moment, he will fear to sin, and be careful in the performance of the commandments - and this is the allusion of the commandment of tzitzit in brief, and the wise will delve into the matters and know them.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:41: And concerning the windings of the tzitzit, they should number thirty-nine [tal], so explained the Ra'aya Meheimna (Parashat Pinchas, page 228b), in these words, on the reason and matter of the commandment, in brief: a third is the knot, and two-thirds are the branch, which is Tiferet. And every winding is threefold, for everything threefold is from the side of holiness, as it is said (in the Kedushah liturgy), "holy" is said three times to You; and Israel is a third, because it is a third over the whole (Exodus 14:7) - for tzitzit is from the side of the central pillar, which is the third of the Patriarchs, and every threefold thing, "Vav-Heh-Vav Yud-Lamed-Yud," every word threefold from its sides - a winding comprised of three threefold windings, this is the Shechinah, "holy is said three times to You," and she is threefold in the central pillar, comprising the three branches of the Patriarchs, which are the "shin" of Shabbat, and the Shechinah is the only daughter, filled with the techelet in the tzitzit. Happy is the body that is thus marked by the Shechinah, and the Holy One, blessed be He, is upon the wings of the commandment - marked in the strap, which is the hand-tefillin, with three windings on the middle finger, corresponding to the winding wound in three windings on the finger. Marked in the knot of the tefillin, comprised of two knots, adding to fifteen threefold - two in one knot. Thirteen windings contain thirty-nine windings, corresponding to the number "tal" [thirty-nine], and thirteen windings correspond to one - together they add to "Ben" [numerically 52], and this is "Ben Yud-Heh," the central pillar - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:42: And there (page 228a) they said that the secret of "tal" [thirty-nine] is Yud-Vav-Dalet Heh-Alef Vav-Alef-Vav, which totals thirty-nine, and the final Heh is the Shechinah, which completes Yud-Heh-Vav-Heh spelled with alefs, which is "Adam." And it appears the intent is toward the allusion of the five knots. And he said afterward, the knot of the tallit is "living forever," for the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah are bound on all sides to the four corners of the tallit - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:43: And there (page 227a) he said that the secret of the tallit is in the secret of Metatron, and Metatron is comprised of four living creatures and six steps to the Throne, and in the Throne there are seventy-two bridges, and corresponding to them there is in the tzitzit an allusion to seventy-two, between the knots and windings, which are thirteen windings and five knots on each side, which are eighteen [chai], and four times eighteen is seventy-two - and so they also explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 10, page 25b) - and this is "and it shall be established in kindness [chesed], a throne" (Isaiah 16:5), for Chesed is seventy-two.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:44: And he said (Ra'aya Meheimna, page 227a) that the allusion of the threads is thirty-two, corresponding to Yud-Heh Heh-Alef, and the Vav-Alef-Vav is the allusion of the thirteen windings, for the completion of "Adam," Yud-Heh-Vav-Heh spelled with alefs, which is in Metatron, whose name is like the name of his Master, and this is his wording: and every living creature has four faces and four wings, which total thirty-two faces and wings, and they depend on the living creature which is Adam, and they are thirty-two, corresponding to the numerical value of Yud-Heh Heh-Alef; the completion, Vav, is thirteen windings on each of the four corners; for the eight threads on each corner correspond to the four faces and four wings of each living creature, which are the four faces of YHVH and the four wings of Adonai - to this point. And afterward he said, we thus find "Yud-Heh-Vav-Heh Adonai" on each side.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:45: And in this very wording he said in the Tikkunim (page 25b): whoever wraps himself in the wrapping of the commandment, it is as though he has established a throne for the Holy One, blessed be He - and these are "Yud-Heh-Vav-Heh Adonai," each totaling four faces and four wings, totaling sixty-four, and the eight letters of "Yud-Heh-Vav-Heh Adonai" total seventy-two - to this point. And he said further afterward (page 26a) that the allusion of the eight threads, corresponding to the four faces and four wings, equals the number of "Shaddai" when spelled out in full.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:46: And further, concerning the allusion of the commandment, it is copied at the end of Parashat Shelach Lecha (page 175a) from the precepts of Rashbi, peace be upon him (cf. Parashat Pinchas, page 257a) - he says there that the secret of the techelet in the tzitzit is the harsh judgment that consumes and destroys everything, and therefore, because of the judgment, it is said (Numbers 15:40), "and you shall see it and remember all My commandments" - like a son who sees the strap and fears to sin against his father because of fear of the strap.
